title: test(plugin-grid): gate the schema-level held-key census on its entry condition
body:
Fixes #7201

Clause-②: no

The schema-level held-key census in `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx` had no expiry gate. Its only pin asserted that the seam **ACCEPTS** `renderCellEditor` and `cellClassName` — true while the keys are held locally and equally true once they arrive through `DeclaredDataTableSchema` — so it stayed green across objectui#6882, the ruling that expired both holds. This transplants the column-level twin (`columnHoldsExpiry-6424.test.ts`) to the sibling census.

Scope is the **narrow shape only**, per the triage ruling in [comment 5530018064](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7201#issuecomment-5530018064). ⛔ No derivation gate over the census — that is the fourth-derivation-gate question the card reserves for a ruling, and the new docblock says so in the tree.

## What landed

`packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/dataTableSchemaSlot-6459.test.ts`, three tests:

1. **The gate.** A compile-time verdict per member of `ObjectGridDataTableSchemaHolds`, recording whether `DataTableSchema` declares that key — plus a pin on the member set itself, so the quantifier is per **HOLD** rather than per key somebody remembered.
2. **Controls on the probe.** The verdict probe shown returning **both** verdicts, in the same query shape: a live declared key (`columns`), a live undeclared one (`accessorKey`, a real key from the column vocabulary next door), and a synthetic one.
3. **A control on the choice of type** — see the second departure below.

`ObjectGrid.tsx`: one census paragraph, comment-only. It said *"Nothing above is mechanically checked, which is how it went stale unseen"*, which this PR falsifies. Leaving that in place would be the exact defect class the card was filed against.

## Two places the transplant is deliberately NOT literal

**1. The probe reads `DeclaredDataTableSchema`, not `DataTableSchema`.** This is the substantive finding of the card, and it is why the obvious gate would not have worked. `DataTableSchema` inherits `BaseSchema`'s string index signature, so `string extends keyof DataTableSchema` and a membership probe against it is **ALWAYS-TRUE** — an instrument with no false to give. Measured, not argued: asserting that a nonsense key is *not* a member of the raw type is red, and green against the stripped type. A gate written the obvious way — asking `DataTableSchema` whether it declares the held key — would be green forever: the same failure this card was filed about, one level up. Pinned as its own control (test 3), so the choice is measured in the tree. `DeclaredDataTableSchema` is `ObjectGrid.tsx`'s own existing strip, so this reuses the repo's machinery rather than adding a second one.

**2. The verdict is recorded per hold, rather than fixed at "is NOT declared".** The card's wording presumes the holds are live. They are not: objectui#6882 declared both keys, and objectui#7196 / PR #7202 already re-derived the prose to say so. A one-directional "is NOT declared" assertion would therefore be **false on this tree for both keys** — a permanently red suite, which cannot land and which no reader can act on. ⛔ Nothing was weakened to make it pass: the precedent itself carries **both** polarities for exactly this reason (`headerIcon` pinned as DECLARED at `:64`, `pinned` as NOT declared at `:138`), because its two keys are in different states. The recorded-verdict form is strictly stronger than the one-directional one — it reddens on the card's event (HELD to DECLARED) **and** on DECLARED to HELD, which is the event that would silently invalidate the "removing these members is inert" measurement objectui#6919 is waiting on. The "is NOT declared" shape is present and live in the suite; it runs on control keys, because there is no hold left to run it on.

## The failure message

The verdict is a string literal, so a flip makes `tsc` print the old and the new one at the failing line, each naming the census prose that then needs re-deriving. Measured output of the first ablation below:

```
dataTableSchemaSlot-6459.test.ts(245,52): error TS2344: Type '"DECLARED by
DataTableSchema — this hold is REDUNDANT. Re-derive the census prose in
ObjectGrid.tsx (the census section, and the ObjectGridDataTableSchemaHolds
docblock under it) before changing anything."' does not satisfy the constraint
'"UNDECLARED by DataTableSchema — this hold is LOAD-BEARING. …"'.
```

An `Expect` of false would only have said that false does not satisfy true.

## The census, re-derived rather than trusted

Counted on the tree at base `045d20ba8`, ⛔ not read off the prose:

| prose claim | measured |
|:--|:--|
| 46 flat-literal keys, 8 group-literal keys | ✅ 46 and 8 exactly, by AST over both annotated literals (47 distinct) |
| the diff now leaves **ZERO** undeclared keys | ✅ all 47 are members of `DeclaredDataTableSchema` (generated per-key probe, compiled clean) |
| each hold member's shape is `Equal` to the upstream declared member | ✅ both, exact in both directions |
| the seam's `renderCellEditor` is the one visible trace — mutually assignable, not `Equal` | ✅ `Equal` is false, mutual assignability true in both directions; the docblock's careful distinction is accurate |
| schema-level `cellClassName` folds at exactly three UTILITY cell sites | ✅ `data-table.tsx` `:2209` selection, `:2226` row-number, `:2554` row-actions; the data cell at `:2312` folds `col.cellClassName` |

⇒ **Every claim held. Nothing was edited to agree with the gate.** The only prose changed is the paragraph this PR itself falsifies.

⚠️ One correction, outside this diff: the triage's third row cites `packages/types/src/data-display.ts:319` and `:504` for the declaration. Those two lines are `TableColumn.cellClassName` and `StaticTableColumn.cellClassName` — the **per-column twins**, on `d04e79a` as well as today. The schema-level declarations the census is about are `:1039` (`renderCellEditor`) and `:1115` (`cellClassName`), both inside `DataTableSchema`. The substance of the claim is unaffected; the citation points at the wrong key, and #7196's whole correction turns on those two `cellClassName`s being different keys that style disjoint cells.

## Reverse verification

Predicted red set first, then mutated. Every mutation proven on disk by anchor counts in **both** directions plus a blob-hash change; every restore proven **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty **and** worktree blob equal to the HEAD blob), never by an exit code. Each leg ran from the committed implementation, under a restore `trap` on `EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths.

⚠️ `packages/plugin-grid/tsconfig.test.json` sets `"paths": {}`, so `@object-ui/types` resolves through `packages/types/dist/*.d.ts`, **not** its source — verified with `--listFiles`. Ablation 1 is therefore rebuilt on both legs and the marker checked into and out of `dist`.

| # | mutation | predicted | measured |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | un-declare schema-level `cellClassName` on `DataTableSchema` (line 1115 only, ⛔ not the column twins), rebuild `packages/types` | the `cellClassName` verdict pin reddens; the acceptance pin above stays green; all controls stay green | ✅ exactly one diagnostic, at the verdict pin, with the message above. Marker into `dist` 1, out 0. **The acceptance pin stayed green — that is the blindness this card is about, reproduced.** |
| 2 | add a third member to `ObjectGridDataTableSchemaHolds` | the member-set pin reddens | ✅ exactly one diagnostic, at that pin |
| 3 | remove `renderCellEditor` from the holds (the objectui#6919 shape) | the verdict pin fails its key constraint **and** the member-set pin reddens | ✅ both, `Type '"renderCellEditor"' does not satisfy the constraint '"cellClassName"'` |

Restores: sources byte-identical to HEAD, `dist` marker back to 0, `dist` real key back to 3, type-check green again.

## Clause-② determination

**Clause-②: no.** Measured, not assumed:

- `ObjectGrid.tsx` is **comment-only** — every added and removed line in that file matches a JSDoc or line-comment shape, zero non-comment lines changed. Declaration emit is a function of the declarations, so the published type surface is unchanged by construction. No key is declared, retired, widened or narrowed anywhere in this diff.
- The suite lives in `src/__tests__/`, which `packages/plugin-grid/tsconfig.json` excludes from the build program by **directory** — re-confirmed green this run by `check:published-tsconfig-exclude` across all 33 enforced packages.
- `packages/types` is what the pin **reads**, ⛔ not what it changes; it is untouched in the final tree.

⇒ Neither what any contract accepts nor the published surface moves. Draft, ⛔ no auto-merge, ⛔ no self-review.

## Verification, on the final commit `016a44c81`

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-grid type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) — **exit 0**
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-grid/` — **112 files, 1012 tests passed**
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-grid lint` — **0 errors** (779 pre-existing warnings; `--max-warnings` is deliberately unset repo-wide)
- `check:control-bytes` ✅ · `check:vi-mock-specifiers` ✅ · `check:vi-mock-inherit` ✅ · `check:phantom-deps` ✅ · `check:published-tsconfig-exclude` ✅ · `check:self-import` ✅
- `check-changeset-presence.mjs` ✅ — empty-frontmatter changeset, the documented exemption for a change that releases nothing

Exit codes captured by redirect-then-read; ⛔ nothing judged through a pipe. Gate results quoted from each gate's own verdict line.

**Declared narrowings** — what was not measured, and what each could have caught:

1. **Repo-wide `pnpm lint` (`turbo run lint`) not run**; `packages/plugin-grid`'s own `eslint .` was, which is the complete population for the only package this diff touches. It could have caught a lint error in another package — but eslint here is **not type-aware** (`tseslint.configs.recommended`, no `project` / `projectService` in `eslint.config.js`), so every rule is file-local and this diff cannot move a verdict on a file it does not contain. No config file and no shared import changed.
2. **Other packages' `type-check` not run.** It could have caught a consumer of `@object-ui/plugin-grid` breaking on a changed exported type — but no exported type changed (comment-only, above), and `packages/types` is untouched in the final tree.
3. **Full-repo `pnpm test` not run.** It could have caught a suite elsewhere that reads these types; the plugin-grid suite that owns them is green in full, and no runtime value changed anywhere in this diff.

CI runs the whole farm regardless; these three are the cheap half deliberately not re-run locally.

## objectui#6919, read before writing — how it bears

#6919 is `pm:blocked`, re-scoped by its PM disposition to the **removal alone**: delete `renderCellEditor` (and any sibling entry now redundant) from `ObjectGridDataTableSchemaHolds`. Its first half — the docblock prohibition — was already discharged by PR #7202. The live blocker is the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` quota, ⛔ not a missing measurement.

It changes this gate in three concrete ways, all handled:

- **It is why the gate is bidirectional.** #6919's whole deliverable rests on "the hold is inert, the members are redundant". If `DataTableSchema` ever stops declaring one of these keys, that measurement silently becomes false and the removal becomes a real narrowing. A one-directional "is NOT declared" pin cannot see that; the recorded verdict does.
- **It will make this suite go red, on purpose.** Removing a member fails the verdict pin's key constraint and moves the pinned member set — ablation 3 above is that exact shape, measured. The docblock carries the one-line replacement (`keyof ObjectGridDataTableSchemaHolds` pinned to `never`) so the removal is a two-line edit, not an obstacle.
- ⛔ **It does not remove a key this gate needs.** The gate is quantified over `keyof ObjectGridDataTableSchemaHolds`, whatever that is on the day. If both members go, the gate becomes the member-set pin alone and still guards the census against a hold silently reappearing.

## Stop-condition

Re-deriving turned up **no further stale claims** beyond the two keys the card names — every prose claim measured above held on `045d20ba8`. #7196's earlier 7-of-16 finding had already been corrected by PR #7202. Nothing was fixed silently; the one triage citation correction is reported above and ⛔ not touched in this diff.
